name: LM7705MM_NOPB
title: LM7705 low-noise negative bias generator, −0.232 V fixed output, 3 V to 5.25 V supply
summary: The LM7705 makes a small fixed negative rail, typically −0.232 V, from one positive supply of 3 V to 5.25 V. Inside, a switched-capacitor inverter sits between a pre-regulator and a post-regulator, so the output is regulated and its ripple is about 4 mVpp; it needs three external capacitors (CFLY, CRES, COUT). It is meant to feed the negative supply pin of a single-supply op amp so the amplifier output can reach true zero volts. It draws 78 µA unloaded at 3.3 V, 20 nA when shut down through its SD pin, comes in an 8-pin VSSOP and is rated from −40 °C to 125 °C.
key_figures: 500 µs typ at 3.3 V, 200 µs at 5 V

notes: The six orderable numbers share the 8-pin VSSOP (DGK) package and the marking F26A; they differ in reel quantity (250, 1000 or 3500). The base device name is LM7705.

circuits.title: Typical application
circuits.description: The LM7705 runs from the same +V rail as a low-voltage op amp and hands it a −0.23 V rail for its negative supply pin, so the amplifier output can swing down to true zero. CFLY across CF+ and CF- is the flying capacitor of the charge pump, CRES from CRES to ground is the reservoir behind the post-regulator, and COUT holds the output. Pulling the shutdown line high turns the bias generator off.
notes: The electrical characteristics are measured with CFLY = 5 µF, CRES = 22 µF and COUT = 22 µF.

circuits.title: True zero output voltage application with or without LM7705
circuits.description: An LMP7701 wired as a voltage follower drives an ADC122S021 12-bit converter. A selector puts the op amp's -V pin either on the LM7705 output (position A, −0.23 V) or on ground (position B), to compare how close to zero the follower output gets in each case. The LM7705 runs from +V with its flying, reservoir and output capacitors.
notes: CRES connects from the CRES pin to ground.

circuits.title: Circuit of the example PCB layout
circuits.description: The LM7705 board behind the example layout. A three-pin header JP3 sets SD either to Vs+ (pins 1-2, the shunt position) or to ground (pins 2-3). VDD is bypassed by 10 µF and 0.1 µF. CFLY is 4.7 µF with a second, unfitted position beside it; CRES is 4.7 µF, again with a spare unfitted position. VOUT carries 470 nF and 22 µF to ground and leaves through a 120 Ω (at 100 MHz) ferrite bead to the output header JP2.

operation.text: A switched-capacitor inverter followed by a regulator gives a fixed, low-noise output of about −0.23 V from a 3 V to 5.25 V supply. A logic low on SD runs the part; a logic high stops it and pulls the output to ground level.

The part works from 3 V to 5.25 V and holds the 3.3-V table limits across that span. Below 3.3 V its output moves toward zero and it can sink less current. Above 5.25 V it is outside its ratings and is damaged.
The pre-regulator ahead of the charge pump and the post-regulator after it together give a line regulation of 0.29 %/V typical.
The output can sink over 26 mA, at which point it has risen to about −200 mV. Up to 20 mA of load the output moves only slightly (load regulation 0.14 %/mA typical at 5 V).
Quiescent current is below 100 µA. Current conversion efficiency is above 90 % from 1 mA of load and reaches 98 % at 5 mA.
SD low: on. SD high: off, with 20 nA supply current. The input thresholds VIL and VIH are higher at VDD = 5 V than at 3.3 V.

An internal oscillator drives two clocks in anti-phase. In the first phase switches S1 and S2 charge CFLY to the supply; in the second, S3 and S4 connect it across CRES with its polarity reversed, so the reservoir sits near minus the supply. This leaves a ripple at the oscillator frequency on the output; it grows with load current and depends on the capacitor values.

Three stages in series: a pre-regulator that meters the power going into the charge pump, the charge-pump inverter itself, and a post-regulator between the pump and the load. The pre-regulator is controlled from the charge pump's output voltage. The post-regulator sets the accurate negative output and acts as a low-pass filter on the switching ripple, which depends on load current and capacitor values.

operation.topic: Why a true-zero amplifier needs a negative rail
operation.text: An op amp output saturates a little above its negative rail: a few hundred millivolts for general-purpose parts, about 200 mV for the LM7332 and 50 mV for the rail-to-rail LMP7701 (10 kΩ load, full temperature). On a single 0/+5 V supply that floor cuts off the bottom of an ADC's range. With a 0 to 90 mV sensor and a gain of 50, the LMP7701 output stops at 50 mV instead of 0 V, losing the lowest 40 codes of a 12-bit, 5 V-reference ADC (1.2 mV steps). In a two-stage chain (gain 10 then 5 from an LMP7702) the first stage's 50 mV floor is multiplied by the second stage to a 500 mV offset, losing about 400 codes.

operation.topic: Negative bias instead of a dual supply
operation.text: A full dual supply removes the floor but costs more and may need op amps rated for the wider total supply. The LM7705 runs from the single positive rail and extends the negative supply by only 0.23 V, enough for a true-zero output from most op amps and in many cases still within the amplifier's maximum supply rating. The total across the amplifier stays below 5.5 V.

With an LMP7701 follower on 5 V and a 50 mVpp input, the converted output bottoms out at 14 mV when the -V pin is grounded (typical VDSAT 18 mV). With the -V pin on the LM7705 output it reaches zero. One-bit steps seen in both records come from ripple and noise; the LM7705 does not add to the quantization error.
A decoupling capacitor goes as close to the VDD pin as possible to keep that pin steady.

Because the part works by shuttling charge among its external capacitors, any resistance in the joints from the pins to those capacitors degrades it. CFLY, CRES and COUT should be low-ESR types on short traces. A small RF capacitor on the output, 100 nF for example, lowers output noise. On the example board the VDD bypass, CFLY, CRES and COUT capacitors are all placed beside the package.
The built-in ESD protection is limited: store and handle with the leads shorted together or in conductive foam to protect the MOS gates.
